title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Which Credits a Settlement Sets Off
content:
*Every credit on the program, or only the recent ones?*

Where credits stand issued on the program in the current billing month and charges also stand on it that
have not fallen due within the ledger window of 24 months, every credit standing on the program is set
off.

Where credits stand issued in the current billing month and no charge stands on it that has not fallen
due within that ledger window, only the credits issued in the current billing month are set off.

In any other case neither term above brings a credit into the set-off.

*Put as a table.*

| Credits issued in the current billing month | Charges standing that have not fallen due within the 24-month ledger window | The credits set off |
|---|---|---|
| some stand | some stand | every credit standing on the program |
| some stand | none stands | only the credits issued in the current billing month |
| none stands | any | neither term above brings a credit into the set-off |

*An illustration.* A rate program under the Demand Service Rate Programs carries credits of 400 US
dollars issued in the current billing month and 250 US dollars issued in an earlier year, and a charge
raised in the billing month that has not fallen due. Every credit standing is set off, so 650 US dollars
comes off. Where no such undue charge stood, only the 400 US dollars of the current billing month would
be set off.
